subject: deep sea dragonfish
title: This Deep-Sea Fish Has Fangs Its Prey Can't See, Even Up Close

scenes.text: This fish has huge fangs. You can't see them.
It's a deep-sea dragonfish, pencil-sized and jet black, hunting about five hundred meters down.
It dangles a glowing lure from its chin. In that glow, ordinary teeth would gleam and give it away.
So its teeth are transparent. They're built from crystals only nanometers wide, too small to scatter light.
And the tips are sharper than a piranha's.
Prey up to half its own size swims toward the light, and never sees the mouth around it.

description:
The deep-sea dragonfish Aristostomias scintillans has oversized fangs that are transparent, so they are almost invisible under water.
A 2019 study in the journal Matter by a University of California San Diego team found why: the outer layer is made of hydroxyapatite nanocrystals and the dentin lacks the microscopic tubules that scatter light in ordinary teeth, so the fangs do not gleam in the glow of the lure on the fish's chin. The tips measure 2.5 to 5 micrometres across, against about 14 for a piranha. The fish, caught about 500 metres down off San Diego, can swallow prey half its own size.
Scariest deep-sea animal you know of? Comment below.
first_comment: The crystals in the teeth are about 20 nanometres across or smaller. Invisible teeth or a glowing lure: which is the better weapon?
